newsitem.title: USA: Massport expected to go to market in late Spring.
newsitem.headline: Massport expected to go to market in late Spring.

text.p: Massport expects to go to the municipal bond market in late Spring, a spokesman for the authority which operates Boston's airport said on Monday.

Noting that the authority was "already a quarter of the way through Logan 2000 (a $1 billion rebuilding and expansion of the city's airport)," Massport spokesman Jeremy Crawford said the agency would be going to the market with an issue in the $200 million to $250 million range "sometime in late Spring."

Under Massachusetts Gov. William Weld's proposal, Massport would be required to kick in $200 million in financing for the $10.7 billion Central Artery/Third Harbor Tunnel project. But a report by the Massachusetts Taxpayers Foundation last Monday projected that even under Weld's proposal to use Massport funds and create a new bonding agency, the state would still fall more than $500 million short in its financing.
Determining the size of Massport's actual contribution to the project, also known as the Big Dig, has caused the agency to re-evaluate the size of its late Spring financing, Crawford said.
But it is the very contribution that causes Moody's Investors Service Corp's analyst Charles Emrich some concern. The rating agency has Massport as an AA rating with a negative outlook.

"One of our concerns is how much of the fiscal autonomy (of Massport) has been compromised," he said in a telephone interview. While acknowledging that Massport will indeed receive some benefit from the Big Dig, Emrich noted that the authority will be "funding something that is not directly related to the agency's activities."

He fears that the $200 million contribution, while only a small part of the authority's $1.75 billion total capital program, will open the door "and set a precedent that Massport will fund other projects in the future that are not directly related to its activities."

Standard & Poor's Corp rates the agency an AA-minus with a developing watch. Fitch Investors Service rates Massport senior revenue debt AA-minus. Analysts from S&P and Fitch were not immediately available for comment.
